MUQATIL:50:39-42/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:50:39-42/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:50:39-42/r1.claim: The Prophet is told to be patient with those saying God rested on the seventh day.

ZAJJAJ:v5p49/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p49/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p49/r3.claim: The praise before sunrise refers to the dawn prayer, and the praise before sunset to the afternoon prayer.

NAHHAS:v4p231/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p231/r8.speaker: أهل التفسير
NAHHAS:v4p231/r8.claim: They say the people addressed are Jews who claimed God rested on the Sabbath; ‘before sunrise and sunset’ means prayer.

NAHHAS:v4p231/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p231/r9.speaker: أهل التفسير
NAHHAS:v4p231/r9.claim: They interpret glorification before sunrise and sunset as prayer.

THALABI:v9p106/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p106/r5.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
THALABI:v9p106/r5.claim: Ata al-Khurasani interprets glorification with praise as saying 'Glory be to God' and 'Praise be to God.'

THALABI:v9p106/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p106/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p106/r6.claim: Other interpreters take glorification as performing prayer with God's command and enabling grace.

THALABI:v9p106/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p106/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v9p106/r7.claim: The prayer before sunrise is the dawn prayer; Ibn Abbas is reported to interpret before sunset as noon and afternoon prayers.

THALABI:v9p106/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p106/r8.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v9p106/r8.claim: Mujahid interprets glorification through the night as night prayer at any time.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p356/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p356/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p356/r4.claim: The Prophet must endure polytheist denial or threats; the instruction applies to his community too.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p356/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p356/r5.speaker: أبو الأحوص
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p356/r5.claim: Glorify God verbally before sunrise and sunset.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p356/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p356/r6.speaker: أبو صالح
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p356/r6.claim: The glorification means dawn and afternoon prayers.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p356/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p356/r7.speaker: جرير بن عبد الله عن النبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p356/r7.claim: Jarir reports the prayer interpretation from the Prophet.

QUSHAYRI:v3p229/r16.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p229/r16.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p229/r16.claim: The Prophet should endure claims about attributes from which God is transcendent and find relief in glorifying Him; solitude at night is clearest.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p416/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p416/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p416/r1.claim: Muqatil says the command to endure what they say concerns the Jews' slander and lies.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p416/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p416/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p416/r2.claim: Muqatil says the verse was revealed about people who mocked the Quran, before the Prophet had permission to fight.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p416/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p416/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p416/r3.claim: Praising God with His praise means performing prayer.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p416/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p416/r4.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p416/r4.claim: Muqatil identifies the prayers before sunrise and sunset as the dawn and afternoon prayers.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p416/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p416/r5.speaker: عطاء والكلبي عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p416/r5.claim: Ata and al-Kalbi transmit from Ibn Abbas an additional identification of the midday prayer.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:50:39-42/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:50:39-42/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:50:39-42/r1.claim: Glorification before sunrise means the dawn prayer; before sunset means noon and afternoon prayers.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p364#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p364#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p364#2/r1.claim: Patience through their denial was commanded before the command to fight.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p364#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p364#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p364#2/r2.claim: Glorifying God with praise means prayer in gratitude; before sunrise is Fajr and before sunset ʿAṣr.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p395/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p395/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p395/r3.claim: “Be patient with what they say” may concern Jewish unbelief and anthropomorphism, or polytheists’ denial of resurrection, since the Creator of the world can resurrect and punish.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p395/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p395/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p395/r4.claim: Some say the patience command was abrogated by the sword verse; another view says patience is commanded in every circumstance.

TABRISI:50:38-40/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:50:38-40/r11.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:50:38-40/r11.claim: He prescribed saying the declaration of God's oneness ten times morning and evening.

TABRISI:50:38-40/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:50:38-40/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:50:38-40/r6.claim: Muhammad is to endure their slander and lies, including calling him a sorcerer or madman, until God brings relief; this was before fighting was commanded.

TABRISI:50:38-40/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:50:38-40/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة وابن زيد
TABRISI:50:38-40/r7.claim: ‘Glorify with praise’ means pray and praise God, since prayer includes glorification and praise.

TABRISI:50:38-40/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:50:38-40/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:50:38-40/r8.claim: Another interpretation is verbal glorification of God, declaring Him above what is unworthy of Him.

TABRISI:50:38-40/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:50:38-40/r9.speaker: قتادة وابن زيد
TABRISI:50:38-40/r9.claim: The times before sunrise and sunset refer to the dawn, noon, and afternoon prayers.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p23/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p23/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p23/r1.claim: The command to endure concerns the opponents' slander and lies.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p23/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p23/r2.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p23/r2.claim: They say the command to be patient was abrogated by the sword verse.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p23/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p23/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p23/r3.claim: Glorifying God with praise means praying while declaring Him exalted above the falsifiers' claims.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p23/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p23/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p23/r4.claim: The prayers before sunrise and sunset are the obligatory noon and afternoon prayers.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p23/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p23/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p23/r5.claim: He identifies the prayer before sunset as the afternoon prayer.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p23/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p23/r6.speaker: جرير بن عبد الله
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p23/r6.claim: In a report in both Ṣaḥīḥ collections, the Prophet likened seeing God to seeing the full moon and urged preserving prayers before sunrise and sunset.

RAZI-FULL:v28p159#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p159#2/r1.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v28p159#2/r1.claim: Earlier commentators explain patience as bearing the talk about exhaustion from reclining; the author instead understands the talk as their claim that resurrection is something astonishing, since Jewish speech is not in this context.

RAZI-FULL:v28p159#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p159#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p159#2/r2.claim: The nearer interpretation is to endure their claim that resurrection is astonishing, because discussion of the Jews' statements has not occurred here.

RAZI-FULL:v28p159#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p159#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p159#2/r3.claim: Tasbīḥ may mean prayer, as in the command to establish prayer at the two ends of the day; before sunrise and before sunset mark those two ends.

QURTUBI-FULL:50:39-40/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:50:39-40/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:50:39-40/r1.claim: The Prophet is told to bear what the polytheists say and let their words weigh lightly on him; the instruction preceded fighting and is said to be abrogated.

QURTUBI-FULL:50:39-40/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:50:39-40/r10.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:50:39-40/r10.claim: Qatāda says he saw no one pray the two pre-Maghrib rakʿahs except Anas and Abū Barza al-Aslamī.

QURTUBI-FULL:50:39-40/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:50:39-40/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:50:39-40/r2.claim: Another view says patience remains binding on the Prophet and his community; another applies it to Jews who said God rested on the Sabbath.

QURTUBI-FULL:50:39-40/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:50:39-40/r3.speaker: أبو صالح
QURTUBI-FULL:50:39-40/r3.claim: He identifies the time before sunrise as the dawn prayer and the time before sunset as the afternoon prayer.

QURTUBI-FULL:50:39-40/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:50:39-40/r4.speaker: جرير بن عبد الله
QURTUBI-FULL:50:39-40/r4.claim: He reports the Prophet's moon analogy for seeing God without crowding, linked to not missing the Fajr and ʿAṣr prayers; Qurtubi says Muslim and Bukhari transmit it.

QURTUBI-FULL:50:39-40/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:50:39-40/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:50:39-40/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets “before sunset” as the noon and afternoon prayers.

QURTUBI-FULL:50:39-40/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:50:39-40/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:50:39-40/r8.claim: Some scholars identify the times as the two pre-dawn rakʿahs and two before Maghrib; Thumāma reports that thoughtful Companions prayed the latter.

QURTUBI-FULL:50:39-40/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:50:39-40/r9.speaker: أنس بن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:50:39-40/r9.claim: In Medina people rushed to mosque pillars for two rakʿahs when the Maghrib call sounded, so a stranger might think the obligatory prayer was already over; Muslim records the report.

BAYDAWI-FULL:50:38-40/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:38-40/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:38-40/r2.claim: Patience is required over polytheists’ denial of resurrection because the Creator can raise and punish them, or over Jews’ disbelief and anthropomorphism.

BAYDAWI-FULL:50:38-40/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:38-40/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:38-40/r3.claim: Glorifying God means declaring Him free of inability and descriptions implying likeness to creation, while praising Him for granting the truth and other blessings.

BAYDAWI-FULL:50:38-40/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:38-40/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:50:38-40/r4.claim: Before sunrise and sunset refers to dawn and afternoon; the two times have known merit.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p175/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p175/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p175/r1.claim: Be patient with the Jews' disbelief and anthropomorphic claims, or the polytheists' talk about resurrection; whoever created the world can raise them and punish them.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p175/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p175/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p175/r2.claim: Tasbīḥ may mean praise while praying; before sunrise refers to Fajr, and before sunset to Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr.

QASHANI:50:37-40/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:50:37-40/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:50:37-40/r4.claim: Patience means annihilation before opponents’ words and restraining the self from displaying its acts, or at least its qualities.

QASHANI:50:37-40/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:50:37-40/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:50:37-40/r5.claim: Praiseful glorification strips ego-qualities and manifests divine qualities and one’s latent perfections in the heart.

QASHANI:50:37-40/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:50:37-40/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:50:37-40/r6.claim: Sunrise and sunset mark spirit’s witnessing and its annihilation in divine unity; night and the aftermath of prostration call for shedding successive ego and heart states after each annihilation.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p409#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p409#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p409#2/r1.claim: The Prophet should patiently bear what the deniers say and withdraw from them graciously.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p409#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p409#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p409#2/r2.claim: Before the Night Journey, the obligatory prayers were two: dawn before sunrise and afternoon before sunset; night vigil was obligatory on the Prophet and community for a year, then abrogated for the community.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p409#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p409#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p409#2/r3.claim: The Night Journey established five prayers, including dawn and afternoon at the times named here.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p409#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p409#2/r4.speaker: جرير بن عبد الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p409#2/r4.claim: The Prophet likened believers’ future sight of their Lord to seeing the full moon without obstruction and urged them to preserve the prayers before sunrise and sunset; the report is in the canonical collections.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p410#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p410#2/r1.speaker: الترمذي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p410#2/r1.claim: Al-Tirmidhi transmits an extra version through Abu Hisham al-Rifa‘i; Ibn Kathir says it is unfamiliar and known only by this route.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p410#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p410#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p410#2/r2.claim: The added material attached to Ibn Abbas’s report is unfamiliar and comes only through this route; Rashidin ibn Kurayb is weak, and the addition may be Ibn Abbas’s own stopped statement.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p265/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p265/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p265/r4.claim: After demonstrating complete knowledge and power, God commands the Prophet to endure everything the disbelievers and others say.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p265/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p265/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p265/r5.claim: Glorifying God with praise affirms every perfection and denies any defect; the opponents’ speech occurs by God’s will.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p265/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p265/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p265/r6.claim: Before sunrise refers to the dawn prayer and other glorification at that time.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p265/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p265/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p265/r7.claim: Before sunset refers to the afternoon and noon prayers, with the afternoon as the time’s principal prayer.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p265/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p265/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p265/r8.claim: The prayer times mark daily activity and return to bodily rest, while also pointing to creation’s folding and resurrection’s raising.

DURR-FULL:v7p610/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p610/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v7p610/r4.claim: The Prophet identifies glorification before sunrise with the dawn prayer and before sunset with the afternoon prayer.

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p199#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p199#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p199#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Jews questioned Muhammad about creation; after he described creation over six days, they said he had answered correctly only if he finished by saying God rested. The Prophet became angry and the verses denying weariness and commanding patience were revealed.

BURSEVI:v9p111#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p111#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p111#2/r1.claim: The preceding verse parallels the proof that the one who created the heavens and earth without fatigue can resurrect the dead; therefore patience is required with deniers of resurrection.

BURSEVI:v9p111#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p111#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p111#2/r2.claim: Patience covers false claims about resurrection from polytheists, Jewish disbelief and anthropomorphism, and other people’s words, since the Creator can resurrect and punish them.

BURSEVI:v9p111#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p111#2/r3.speaker: المناسبات
BURSEVI:v9p111#2/r3.claim: The commentary on coherence links patience to God’s encompassing knowledge and power: His awareness of enemies’ acts warns them and consoles His allies.

BURSEVI:v9p111#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p111#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p111#2/r4.claim: Ishari reading: patience with ignorant people’s hurtful words disciplines the self and purges blameworthy traits, alongside constant remembrance and praise.

BURSEVI:v9p111#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p111#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p111#2/r5.claim: Glorification denies that God is incapable or breaks His promises, including the resurrection, or can be described anthropomorphically; praise thanks Him for guidance and other blessings.

BURSEVI:v9p111#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p111#2/r6.speaker: سهل
BURSEVI:v9p111#2/r6.claim: Sahl says praise accompanies glorification because reason establishes God’s existence and removes created attributes, while revelation then teaches His names and attributes and adds praise.

BURSEVI:v9p111#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p111#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p111#2/r7.claim: ‘Before sunrise’ and ‘before sunset’ refer to the Fajr and Asr prayers, whose excellence is well known.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p192#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p192#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p192#2/r1.claim: Be patient with polytheists' denials of resurrection: the One who created the world rapidly can resurrect and punish them.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p192#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p192#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p192#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, endure the Jews' blasphemous and anthropomorphic claims.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p192#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p192#2/r3.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v26p192#2/r3.claim: Al-Kashf says the first reading connects the command to the sūra's opening through this point, fitting the continuous argument better than attaching it only to the immediately preceding creation statement.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p192#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p192#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p192#2/r4.claim: Al-Ālūsī considers the nearer connection to be with the preceding creation statement on either interpretation.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p192#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p192#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p192#2/r5.claim: Glorify God as free of incapacity and of breaking His promise of resurrection, and of any likeness to creation; it can also mean all imperfections while praising Him for guidance and other favors.

ALUSI-FULL:v26p192#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v26p192#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v26p192#2/r6.claim: Sunrise and sunset denote the times of the Fajr and ʿAṣr prayers, whose virtue is well known.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p326/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p326/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p326/r2.claim: The command to be patient follows the preceding discourse and consoles the Prophet amid denial of resurrection and his message; “what they say” gathers both charges.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p326/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p326/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p326/r3.claim: The pronoun in “they say” refers to the polytheists addressed by the admonitions beginning with their surprise at a warner from among themselves.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p326/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p326/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p326/r4.claim: The author recounts that ʿUqba b. Abi Muʿayṭ put camel entrails on the Prophet while he prostrated; Abu Bakr pulled him away and invoked the case of a man who says “My Lord is God.”

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p326/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p326/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p326/r5.claim: The author also connects the mockery of worshippers to the Quranic rebuke of one who forbids a servant from praying.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p326/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p326/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p326/r6.claim: Tasbih here means prayer, as Ibn ʿAṭiyya says exegetes unanimously held; the verb becomes intransitive like “pray,” and “with praise” fits recitation of al-Fatiha in each unit.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p326/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p326/r7.speaker: جرير بن عبد الله
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p326/r7.claim: In a report in Sahih Muslim, the Prophet likens seeing God to seeing the moon and urges preserving prayer before sunrise and sunset, identified as dawn and afternoon prayers.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p326/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p326/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p326/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas identifies the prayer before sunset as noon and afternoon prayers.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p326/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p326/r9.speaker: قتادة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p326/r9.claim: Qatada identifies the prayer before sunset as the afternoon prayer.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p327/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p327/r1.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p327/r1.claim: Most exegetes understand night-time tasbih as prayer; Abu al-Aḥwaṣ instead takes it as saying “Glory be to God.”

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p327/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p327/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p327/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies the night prayers as Maghrib and ʿIsha.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p327/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p327/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p327/r3.claim: The span before sunset begins when the sun passes its zenith and ends at sunset, covering noon and afternoon prayer; night prayer means Maghrib and ʿIsha, since the night began at sunset in their calendar.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p327/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p327/r4.speaker: أبو برزة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p327/r4.claim: An alternative takes all the times as supererogatory prayers: two units before sunrise and two before sunset.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p327/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p327/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p327/r5.claim: On the supererogatory-prayer interpretation, Mujahid identifies the night prayer as night vigil.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p327/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p327/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p327/r6.claim: This alternative raises whether the command recommends prayers generally or imposes them specifically on the Prophet; the author points ahead to Surat al-Muzzammil.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p327/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p327/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v26p327/r7.claim: The author links the prayer schedule to the commands in al-Insan and al-Tur.

TABATABAI:50:39-42/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:50:39-42/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:50:39-42/r1.claim: The conclusion tells Muhammad to endure accusations of sorcery, madness, and poetry, as well as mockery of resurrection, while awaiting the trumpet and warning the God-fearing.

TABATABAI:50:39-42/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:50:39-42/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:50:39-42/r2.claim: The patience command follows all the preceding denials of resurrection, proof of it, and warnings about earlier peoples who rejected their prophets.

TABATABAI:50:39-42/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:50:39-42/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:50:39-42/r3.claim: Glorifying before sunrise can correspond to dawn prayer; before sunset can correspond to afternoon prayer or to afternoon and noon prayers.

ASAD-NOTES:50:39#n30/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:50:39#n30/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:50:39#n30/r1.claim: The instruction to bear patiently concerns claims that resurrection is impossible.

ASAD-NOTES:50:39#n31/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:50:39#n31/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:50:39#n31/r1.claim: Glorifying God before sunrise and sunset means remembering His almightiness throughout the day.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p435/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p435/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p435/r1.claim: The Prophet is to persevere in truth and seek perseverance from God through prayer.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p435/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p435/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p435/r2.claim: He should leave his enemies' case to the certain Day of Judgement.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p461/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p461/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p461/r4.claim: The Prophet should patiently endure opposition and diligently maintain prayer.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p464/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p464/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p464/r1.claim: God’s lack of weariness after creating the heavens and earth assures the Prophet that resurrection will occur and he should endure what opponents say.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p464/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p464/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p464/r5.claim: The objections to endure include the denial of resurrection in 50:2–3; this purposeful world will fulfill its end, though dead-hearted people will believe only upon seeing it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p465/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p465/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p465/r1.claim: Prayer is the means of gaining patience amid opposition: reliance on God enables perseverance, and patience itself requires God’s help, as 16:127 says.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p465/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p465/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p465/r2.claim: Tasbīḥ negates what is unworthy of God and ḥamd affirms attributes befitting Him; together they establish sound knowledge of God and ground patience and trust.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p465/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p465/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p465/r3.claim: Constant remembrance enlivens and comforts the heart, while designated worship times coincide with cosmic changes that display God’s greatness.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p465/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p465/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p465/r4.claim: Before sunrise means fajr and before sunset means ʿaṣr; dawn and the sun’s decline display cosmic submission, and Qur’an and Hadith emphasize both prayers.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p466/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p466/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p466/r2.claim: Prayer order reflects religious importance: fajr first, then ʿaṣr, followed by night prayers, with ẓuhr and maghrib after the sun’s prostration; this covers all five prayers.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p467/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p467/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p467/r1.claim: The parallel in 20:130 presents the same call to patience and glorification at appointed times; the details are discussed in the commentary on Ṭāhā.

STUDYQURAN:50:39/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:50:39/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:50:39/r1.claim: The call to patience addresses the Prophet and, by extension, all Muslims, urging endurance of the chiding of disbelievers and naysayers.

STUDYQURAN:50:39/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:50:39/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:50:39/r2.claim: Praising God means turning to Him instead of dwelling on disbelievers' words.

STUDYQURAN:50:39/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:50:39/r3.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:50:39/r3.claim: Some commentators identify the time before sunrise as the morning prayer and before sunset as the late afternoon prayer.

STUDYQURAN:50:39/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:50:39/r4.speaker: JJ, Z
STUDYQURAN:50:39/r4.claim: Other commentators say that “before the setting” refers to both afternoon prayers.

STUDYQURAN:50:39/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:50:39/r5.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:50:39/r5.claim: On a full-moon night, the Prophet told Companions that they would see their Lord as plainly as the moon and urged them not to miss the dawn and afternoon prayers.
